env.world:
The observable Gaussian covariance experiment attached to a paired model. Each environment law is \(P_{M,e}=\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_{M,e})\) with \(\Sigma_{M,e}\) symmetric positive definite, and the observed parameter is the stacked half-vector \(s(M)=\operatorname{vech}( oldsymbol\Sigma_M)\in\Omega_p=\operatorname{vech}(\operatorname{PD}_p)^2\subseteq\mathbb R^{d}\), \(d=p(p+1)\). Partial regression coefficients are \(r_e(A,B\mid S)=\Sigma_{e,AB\cdot S}/\Sigma_{e,BB\cdot S}\); recording, for every ordered pair \(A,B\) and every \(S\subseteq\mathbb V\setminus\{A,B\}\), whether \(r_1=r_2\), together with the separating sets used by population LDiffPC, gives the complete ledger \(\mathcal L(s)\) and the population output graph \(H(s)\); the compatible-completion fiber is \(\mathfrak F(s)\) and its effect fiber is \(\Psi(s)=\overline{\{	au(M):M\in\mathfrak F(s)\}}\subseteq\mathbb R^3\). Sampling: conditionally on \(M\), the data are \(\mathcal Z_n=((Z_{ei})_{i\le n_e})_{e=1,2}\) with joint law \(P_{M,1}^{n_1}\otimes P_{M,2}^{n_2}\), \(n_1,n_2>p\); with \(
u_e=n_e-1\) the sample covariances are \(\widehat\Sigma_e=
u_e^{-1}\sum_i(Z_{ei}-\overline Z_e)(Z_{ei}-\overline Z_e)^{\mathsf T}\). The exact pivot is \(T_{e,n}(S)=
u_e\{\operatorname{tr}(S^{-1}\widehat\Sigma_e)-\log\det(S^{-1}\widehat\Sigma_e)-p\}\), calibrated by the \(a\)-quantile \(q_{p,
u}(a)\) of the same functional of a \(\operatorname{Wishart}_p(I_p,
u)\) matrix; at miscoverage \(\gamma\in(0,1/2)\) and \(a_\gamma=\sqrt{1-\gamma}\) the region is \(\mathcal R_{n,\gamma}=\prod_{e}\{S_e\succ0:T_{e,n}(S_e)\le q_{p,
u_e}(a_\gamma)\}\) and the reported set is \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\gamma}=\overline{ igcup_{s:\operatorname{vech}^{-1}(s)\in\mathcal R_{n,\gamma}}\Psi(s)}\), with the bounded-subclass analogue \(\widehat{\mathcal C}^{B}_{n,\gamma}\) obtained by projecting the same region through \(\Psi_B\). A competitor is any sequence \((D_N)\) of closed random subsets of \(\mathbb R^3\) measurable with respect to \(\mathcal Z_n\).

env.world: The local covariance experiment at a boundary point. Fix \(s_0\in\Omega_p\) and let \(\{\mathcal S_b\}_{b\in\mathbb B_p}\) be the finite family of semialgebraic covariance cells produced by enumerating baseline graphs, target sets, common orders, difference DAGs, exact-ledger sign patterns, LDiffPC-compatible orientations and Cholesky cases, each carrying its rational predecessor-regression target map \(\theta_b:\mathcal S_b\to\mathbb R^3\). The accessible branches are \(\mathbb B(s_0)=\{b:s_0\in\overline{\mathcal S_b}\}\), their tangent cones are \(T_b(s_0)=\operatorname{Tan}(\overline{\mathcal S_b},s_0)\), and \(\Gamma(s_0)=\{\theta_b(s_0):b\in\mathbb B(s_0)\}\). Local alternatives are indexed by \(h\in\mathbb R^d\) along \(N^{-1/2}\)-local model sequences \((M_N)\) with \(s(M_N)=s_0+h/\sqrt N+o(N^{-1/2})\) inside one branch. Writing \(\lambda=\lim n_1/N\in(0,1)\) and \(V(\Sigma)_{AB,CD}=\Sigma_{AC}\Sigma_{BD}+\Sigma_{AD}\Sigma_{BC}\) in half-vector coordinates, the limit noise is \(\mathbb Z_0\sim\mathcal N(0,V_0)\) with \(V_0=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda^{-1}V(\Sigma_{0,1}),(1-\lambda)^{-1}V(\Sigma_{0,2}))\), and the acceptance body \(\mathcal A_\gamma(h+\mathbb Z_0)\) is the product over \(e=1,2\) of covariance-score ellipsoids centred at the corresponding block, each of \(\chi^2_{p(p+1)/2,\sqrt{1-\gamma}}\) radius. The zeroth- and first-order limits are \(\mathcal K^{(0)}_h=\{\theta_b(s_0):b\in\mathbb B(s_0),\ T_b(s_0)\cap\mathcal A_\gamma\neq\varnothing\}\) and \(\mathcal K^{(1)}_h=\bigcup_b D\theta_b(s_0)\bigl(T_b(s_0)\cap\mathcal A_\gamma\bigr)\), with the regular-stratum image \(\mathcal P_\gamma(y;b_0,s_0)=J(T_{b_0}(s_0)\cap\mathcal A_\gamma(y))\), \(J=D\theta_{b_0}(s_0)\). When \(\Gamma(s_0)=\{\tau_0\}\), \(\tau_0\) is the common accessible-branch target. Convergence of random closed sets is taken in the Fell topology.

env.world: The bounded Gaussian tangent decision problem at a boundary point with \(\Gamma(s_0)=\{\tau_0\}\). Fix a localization radius \(R\in(0,\infty)\) and set \(\Lambda_R=\{(b,h):b\in\mathbb B(s_0),\ h\in T_b(s_0),\ \|h\|_2\le R\}\). Under local direction \(h\) one observes \(\mathbb Y_h=h+\mathbb Z_0\sim\mathcal N(h,V_0)\), and the branch target is the linear functional \(\eta_b(h)=D\theta_b(s_0)h\in\mathbb R^3\). A decision rule is an Effros-measurable randomized map \(\delta:\mathbb R^d\times[0,1]\to\mathcal F(\mathbb R^3)\) into the closed subsets of \(\mathbb R^3\), where \(U\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) is independent of \(\mathbb Y_h\) for every \(h\). The loss is the extended diameter, with \(\operatorname{diam}(C)=0\) when \(C\) is empty or a singleton and \(\operatorname{diam}(C)=\sup_{x,y\in C}\|x-y\|_2\in[0,\infty]\) otherwise. The admissible class is \(\mathfrak D_R=\{\delta:\inf_{(b,h)\in\Lambda_R}\Pr_h[\eta_b(h)\in\delta(\mathbb Y_h,U)]\ge1-\gamma\}\), the risk is \(\mathfrak R_R(\delta)=\sup_{(b,h)\in\Lambda_R}\mathbb E_h[\operatorname{diam}(\delta(\mathbb Y_h,U))]\), and the value is \(v_R=\inf_{\delta\in\mathfrak D_R}\mathfrak R_R(\delta)\).

decisions: No paper manifest (`state.theorems`) was supplied in the brief, so no `theorem_local_id` was set on any statement node and no `theorems` manifest is emitted.
`design_decisions` was empty and `Added assumptions` was empty, so no scope simplification was applied; every core node is mapped.

`ThreeVariableIdentifiedEffectSet` is a dimension-scoped notation for `IdentifiedEffectSet` at p = 3 (the core describes it that way and gives it no definition node), so it is bound in S2 and realized as the p = 3 instance of `identifiedEffectSet` rather than as a separate Lean object.
`RegressionCoefficient` has no definition node of its own; it is introduced inside `def:exact-ledger`, which is the only place the core defines it.

For `thm:honesty-noncontraction-lower-bound` and `thm:collider-witness-audit`, `def:boundary-model-class` is listed in `hyps` to satisfy the deterministic assumption-coverage check, but semantically it is a conclusion-side membership predicate (the theorems PROVE their witnesses belong to the class). This is flagged in each node's `notes` so F2 does not emit it as a binder.

Cited gates are threaded only into consumers that list them in `depends_on` (P4 forbids `hyps` outside `depends_on`). Transitive consumers -- notably `thm:finite-sample-honesty` and `thm:bounded-projected-wishart-constant-factor-minimax`, which use `lem:true-completion-retention` -- inherit the gate through that lemma's own binder; F2 must thread it when instantiating.

`lem:prokhorov-tightness`, `lem:portmanteau-usc` and `lem:standard-borel-disintegration` have exact or near-exact Mathlib counterparts (`isCompact_closure_of_isTightMeasureSet`, `ProbabilityMeasure.limsup_measure_closed_le_of_tendsto`, `Measure.condKernel`/`disintegrate`). Per the F1 rules a frozen `status:"cited"` node is never converted to a non-gate form here; the counterparts are recorded in `notes` as small-effort candidates for the later `bin/gate.ts --discharge` path.
